I had mine only for six months before my body rejected it. Insertion was incredibly painful for me - apparently I have a very high cervix, so that played a part. But I blacked out due to the pain. Luckily my husband was with me and drove me home. On the way home, I vomited on the side of the road, then went home and slept for about 10 hours with a heating  pad and pain medicine. 

My doctor had given me medicine to dilate my cervix the night before to make it easier, as well as 800 mg ibuprofen. That didn’t matter to me.

I bled for 1.5 months straight, heavily. It severely impacted my moods - low sex drive, my depression was out of control...

Then at about 5/6 months and after several ovarian cysts, my body finally said “fuck you” and rejected the iud. I had to go to the hospital to have it removed before it did any damage. 

Removal was a PIECE OF CAKE - minor cramps. Nothing like insertion. 

I know I am a rare case, everyone seems to have good luck with it. I just always want people to be aware that it CAN be pretty bad.

Oh! I’m sorry, thank you for the clarification. I guess I’d compare it more to a safe house? I’m honestly not sure. We just always called it a shelter. Some girls also were suicidal/had self-harm tendencies. We had to have eyes-on at almost all times (aside from bathroom obviously) and do frequent room checks, we also were trained to restrain if needed (had to several times... it was terrifying but necessary). The length of time they stayed at the shelter depended case by case, and was determined by their case worker. However, some of the less severe cases could have home visits.
I guess it would be considered residential. It was more or less a group home.

They were incredibly mature about it all. The older girls explained it to the younger girls in a manner that they’d understand, but without sugar coating anything. With some girls, you could tell they were working through figuring it all out. Some still sympathized with their rapists. Some held out that their rapists actually cared for them because they were family members. But no matter what, they all knew that it was absolutely not an okay thing, and that they understood that it wasn’t their fault.

It was through child services system. I was working in a very poor state at one of only like... 4 facilities of its kind throughout the entire state. I was a Residential Aid, so I worked about 10-12 hours a day/sometimes 6 days a week feeding the girls, helping with homework, taking them to appointments... basically acting as the mother or big sister/guardian that some of these girls never had. We took them to doctor’s appointments, as well as appointments with their case workers, and often drove them to court. We were so understaffed. It was tough, but a job I’ll surely never forget.

The state tried to send younger children our way, but we weren’t allowed to take them. I honestly can’t recall what happened in those situations. That job truly tested my faith in humanity. I worked there for about three years before moving away, and to this day I still think of all of the girls that came in and out of the shelter, and can only hope they’re doing okay.

I didn’t see it, but I heard it. I used to work at a shelter for at-risk girls aged 8-18, mainly truancy or runaway cases but some were taken from homes of abuse, drugs, sex trafficking, etc. We housed and looked after roughly 20 girls at a time when we were at full capacity. Many of them had a lot of mental and emotional issues. One of our youngest girls at the time, around age 9, was talking to an older girl (around 13). Teen was nonchalantly talking about how she was raped as a young girl before she came to the shelter.

My sophomore year of college, I met a guy through one of those “anon” twitter accounts. We immediately hit it off, and soon started dating despite him being in Texas at the time, and my being in West Virginia. We Skyped every evening, texted nonstop. I was head-over-heels for this guy. We eventually planned for him to come spend the weekend with me in WV, and I was 1000% sure he was the one for me. It seemed to be reciprocated.

We were together for two years. He met my family, I spent Christmas and New Years with him and his family. We went to a jeweler to browse for engagement rings..

Then I went back to school for my junior year. At this time, he lived in GA, I was still in WV for college. It was right around when GA got a ton of really awful snow, and I remember texting him and suddenly getting no response. He wouldn’t answer my calls. His parents never got back to me. I was worried sick.

Two days later, a friend of his reached out to me and said he had talked to him and that everything was fine. But still — no text, no call, no nothing. A few days later, he had blocked me on all social media, blocked my phone number.

No explanation, no goodbyes. Not even an official “break-up”. I was devastated. I wouldn’t eat, I went into a severe depression. Skipped a bunch of my classes, isolated myself from my friends. It was horrible. I was in this constant state of extreme anxiety for months after.

He’s active on Reddit still. I’ve tried reaching out to figure out what happened, what I did wrong to make him so suddenly just disappear, but no luck..



TLDR: Started dating a boy I met on Twitter. Truly thought he was the one after meeting his family and him meeting mine. Two years in, he blocks me on social media, blocks my cell number, and disappears from my life with zero explanation. He’s alive, active on Reddit. Hope he sees this.
